flags: minor: wrong choices are weak; only C ('improvement on', via the new wiring) has any pull
S031-01.notes: The ceiling and balconies were reproduced exactly and only hidden systems changed, so the theater is faithful to the original. A and D contradict 'exactly'. C goes against the point that the visible work was copied, not improved.

flags: minor: 'only after the community had built' signals 'conditional' almost word for word, so this is a near-lookup
S031-02.notes: The return depends on a condition (storage being built first), so the offer is conditional. 'Immediate' contradicts this, and nothing supports 'irrevocable' or 'unprecedented'.

flags: minor: the word 'alone' in the stem lines up only with D, which gives a shortcut
S031-03.notes: The pollen evidence offers a rival explanation, so timing by itself does not prove human blame. B is the trap: it overclaims that food loss was 'most likely' the cause, when the text only raises it as possible. A and C go against the text.

flags: minor: D only restates a fact already in the passage, so it is weak as a distractor
S031-04.notes: If the crows also avoid a matching park where no trapping happened, the avoidance points to the park's features, which weakens the hypothesis. B (social learning) fits the hypothesis and is the main trap. A, with avoidance fading over time, is also consistent with a learned link to danger.

S031-05.notes: Dry season: 96-75=21 points. Rainy season: 97-93=4 points. Both differences check out. A is the only choice that compares the effect of cleaning across the two seasons. B, C and D are true but do not address the size of the difference.

flags: minor: D closely paraphrases the last sentence of Text 2 ('recording what was thought to be known... more than... marking danger'), so the item is close to a lookup
S031-06.notes: The historian says the creatures recorded what was thought to be known rather than warning of danger. B is the nearest distractor: the creatures did come from earlier books, but Text 2 never says they were copied 'without regard to their meaning'. A and C are not supported.

S031-07.notes: The audience is unfamiliar with qanats, so the sentence must say what a qanat is as well as state the advantage. B does both. A gives the advantage but no definition, and it is the trap. C and D give no advantage.

S031-08.notes: The sentence moves from the usual cooling gas, which this eruption released little of, to what it released in its place (water vapor), so 'Instead' fits. 'Similarly' and 'For this reason' get the logic wrong, and 'Specifically' does not fit. Fact check: the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption did inject a record amount of water vapor with little SO2, and scientists did raise the possibility of temporary warming. Accurate.

S031-09.notes: The list items contain internal commas, and the later items are already separated by a semicolon, so a semicolon is needed after 'Iceland'. A is the trap (a comma makes the list ambiguous). B and D are wrong.

S031-10.notes: The subject 'Sylvia Earle' needs a finite main verb after the relative clause, so 'founded' is correct. A, B and C all leave the sentence without a main verb. Facts: Earle founded Mission Blue in 2009 (with her TED Prize), and she has led more than 100 expeditions. Accurate.
